title: Who has the edge in Miami vs. Notre Dame? Position-by-position breakdown - CBS Sports
description: The tale of the tape for this heavyweight Week 10 matchup, with a deep dive into which team has the advantage at
body:
The tale of the tape for this heavyweight Week 10 matchup, with a deep dive into which team has the advantage at every position group
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:32 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One year ago, a 27-24 Week 1 loss at Miami came back to haunt a Notre Dame team that was left on the doorstep of the College Football Playoff in favor of the Hurricanes because of that head-to-head result. Now, more than 14 months after their fateful road loss to the 'Canes, the Fighting Irish finally get their chance at revenge.No. 11 Notre Dame is hosting No. 1 Miami on Saturday night in a battle overflowing with storylines. First and foremost, the postseason fates of both teams hang in the balance. Neither one of these teams wants to tempt fate and arrive at Selection Sunday with two losses, and Notre Dame already has one.Then, there is the sheer revenge factor. The Miami loss was the lone obstacle between Notre Dame and a spot in the 12-team field on Selection Sunday in 2025. For the Hurricanes, this is an opportunity to take a vice grip on the No. 1 spot in the CFP Rankings while showcasing the Heisman candidacy of star quarterback Darian Mensah.But if Notre Dame can slay Miami, it will mark just the second time in college football history that an AP top-2 team will have lost in five straight weeks. In what's been a season of chaos, this matchup is guaranteed to provide more.
Here is the position-by-position breakdown of the heavyweight Week 10 battle.
        
            
                College Football Playoff Rankings reaction: Notre Dame among underrated teams slighted, SEC's efforts succeed
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Quarterback Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is dealing with a problematic case of inaccuracy on downfield throws. Over the Fighting Irish's past two games, he is just 4 for 24 on passes traveling 15+ air yards. Contrast that to the season's first six games, when he was 21 of 39 on such attempts, and it's clear something has changed.Miami's Darian Mensah is the national leader in passing efficiency and completion percentage (80.7%) and has been firmly No. 1 in the CBS Sports QBPR for several weeks. The Duke transfer has upgraded Miami's offense and can bolster an already-strong Heisman Trophy case with a strong performance. Edge: MiamiSkill talent Malachi Toney's ankle injury drastically alters the calculus of this debate. The shifty speedster is expected to miss several games after undergoing surgery. However, Miami's secondary pass-catchers are solid, too. Duke transfer Cooper Barkate finished second in the ACC in receiving yards last season behind only Toney, and he has great chemistry with Mensah. Tight end Elija Lofton has also established himself as a reliable weapon.
Senior receiver Jordan Faison is on track for a career year with Notre Dame, and with Toney out of the picture, the Fighting Irish's pass-catching crew is about equal to Miami's group. Where Miami gets a slight edge is at running back. Notre Dame's ground game is improving behind the trio of Nolan James Jr., Jonas Walton and Aneyas Williams. But Miami's duo of Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory is one of the nation's best as Mallory continues to shine during a breakout freshman season. Edge: MiamiMiami receiver Malachi Toney will miss Miami's game against Notre Dame after undergoing ankle surgery. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Offensive line Notre Dame leads the FBS with just two sacks allowed. The Fighting Irish are allowing pressure on just 19.1% of dropbacks, which is No. 2 nationally. Miami's offensive line has been solid, too, surrendering just 10 sacks and allowing pressure on only 25.5% of dropbacks. But Notre Dame's pass protection is as good as it gets in college football. Both teams get good run blocking and average 5+ yards per carry. The Fighting Irish get the nod because they are reliable at keeping Carr upright. Edge: Notre Dame
Front seven Miami's defense remains strong, but Akheem Mesidor and Rueben Bain Jr. aren't walking through that door. The fierceness of the 'Canes front seven is down a few notches without those two stars, who were each first-round picks in the 2026 NFL Draft. After ranking fourth in the FBS in pressure rate at 40.7% last season, the Hurricanes are 26th entering this game at 35.5%. Notre Dame is in the same neighborhood at 34.2%, but the Fighting Irish have not blitzed as much.Both rank in the top 10 in terms of yards allowed per rushing attempt, making this a wash. Edge: evenSecondary Opposing passers have a much better efficiency rating (134.7) against Miami than they do against Notre Dame (119.0). The Fighting Irish are surrendering just 6.2 yards per pass attempt while Miami's opposition is averaging 7.1 yards per attempt. Notre Dame also has eight interceptions compared to Miami's four.
Getting things done through the air has been more practical against the Hurricanes, in part, because teams have generally been playing from behind. Miami has also faced Wake Forest star quarterback Gio Lopez and played a dialed-in version of North Carolina's Billy Edwards Jr. last week. When Notre Dame played UNC, rain interfered with the Tar Heels' aerial attack. The advantage here is in Notre Dame's favor, although Miami's passing game will be the best Notre Dame's defense has seen. Edge: Notre DameCoaching Marcus Freeman showed the ability to win "the big one" a few times in 2024 as the Fighting Irish won three playoff games that season before faltering against Ohio State in the national title game. Similarly, Miami's Mario Cristobal broke through last season by leading the Hurricanes to a title-game appearance. From a coordinator perspective, Hurricanes OC Shannon Dawson has been elite this year, showing the ability to scheme up innovative ways to get the football into Malachi Toney's hands. Because of Dawson's influence, Miami gets the nod on the coaching side. Edge: MiamiFinal tallyCategoryNotre DameMiamiQB✅Skill✅OL✅Front 7━━Secondary✅Coaching✅

        The NFL season reaches its unofficial midway point this weekend, and teams hoping to be relevant for the final two months of the regular season are seeing their margin for error shrink and shrink exponentially.No division is better -- or more competitive -- than the NFC North, where the team in last, the 5-3 Packers, would be in the playoffs if they started today. The NFC North has a legitimate shot to be the first division in the current conference alignment to put four teams in the playoffs, but given how tough the in-division games will be, none of them can afford many slip-ups outside the division. Green Bay has done a terrific job rallying from an uninspiring 1-2 start to put themselves in a position to be relevant. But, as we'll see, that's still a precarious position.Using SportsLine's projections, we take a look at what's on the line for the five most important games of the weekend and how their results will impact the playoff picture.1. Packers at PatriotsSunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free)PackersPatriotsCurrent playoff chance56%63%With win67%73%With loss46%51%After unsteady starts from both teams, the Patriots and Packers would both be in the playoffs if they started today ...  but only as the No. 7 seeds in their respective divisions.But the playoffs don't start today. In fact, we're only just now reaching the halfway point of the regular season. That makes this showdown between big-play quarterbacks Jordan Love and Drake Maye a huge one. After a relatively easy stretch, the Patriots have a tough stretch -- Packers, at Lions, at Chargers, Bills, Vikings, at Chiefs -- upcoming. The Packers, meanwhile, go at Patriots, Vikings, at Rams.One of these teams will enter the second half of the season feeling really good. The other? Not so much.2. Rams at CommandersSunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free)RamsCommandersCurrent playoff chance28%31%With win39%42%With loss18%22%It's not quite an elimination game -- we're still way too early for that -- but the 4-4 Rams dropping below .500 would be a massive blow for the preseason Super Bowl favorites. Los Angeles has won two straight and should make it three in a row. There just isn't enough room for error left for the Rams, especially when they're favored.The Commanders, meanwhile, are just kind of sticking around in the lowly NFC East. A Week 10 game against the Giants will be crucial, but if they can spring an upset before that, it'd be a nice boost for their postseason hopes.3. Buccaneers at BearsSunday, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC (Stream: fubo, try for free)BuccaneersBearsCurrent playoff chance54%87%With win67%92%With loss48%77%For the third straight week, the Bears are on primetime, and if it goes half as well as Monday night's statement blowout of the Seahawks did, Chicago will win its fourth straight and move to 7-2.But let's not just hand this one to Caleb Williams and co. The Buccaneers have won three of four after a nightmarish 0-4 start and now look like a potential frontrunner in the NFC South. Tampa Bay's turnaround has been fueled by a dominant running game and terrific defense.Both of these teams are in competitive division races, but for very different reasons. The NFC North is historically great. The NFC South is awful. That means big implications.4. Cardinals at SeahawksSunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free)CardinalsSeahawksCurrent playoff chances2%58%With win6%38%With loss1%63%Similar to the Rams, the Seahawks (also 4-4) wouldn't be completely out of it with a loss, but it would be a devastating early blow. The reigning champs simply have to take care of business in games like these. That's what happens when you have a slow start: Your back is starting to get close to the wall by November.
The Cardinals, meanwhile, are looking to play spoiler, and if we learned anything from last week's Gardner Minshew-led comeback win over the Cowboys, it's that Arizona is more than happy to do just that. Seattle's defense, though, is an entirely different beast.5. Bengals at Falcons (in Spain)Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network (Stream: fubo, try for free)BengalsFalconsCurrent playoff chances89%21%With win93%30%With loss83%15%The NFL's international games continue after a one-week break, and it's a big chance for both teams. The Bengals can keep up in the AFC North, while the Falcons can get back into the win column and stay right in the thick of the NFC South race. Considering both the Buccaneers (at Bears) and the Panthers (vs. Broncos) both have tough tasks, the Falcons going abroad and coming back with a win would be a huge result.

title: Week 9 Super Bowl stock report: Jeffery Simmons trade legitimizes Bears, QB injuries tank Ravens - CBS Sports
description: We assess the NFL title race after Week 8 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl pic
body:
We assess the NFL title race after Week 8 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture

    8:09 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away, so a flurry of impactful moves could be on the way as Super Bowl contenders gear up for the stretch run. Even if the biggest transactions are already complete, this year's deadline will go down as a significant one, because the Chicago Bears proved in Week 8 how the acquisition of one star can flip a season. Jeffery Simmons elevated their defense in his first game following last week's blockbuster trade and rounded the Bears into an even more legitimate championship hopeful.The Baltimore Ravens just made a move themselves at quarterback, but it doesn't come close to lifting the team the way Simmons does. Their top two options sustained injuries last week that could hold both of them out for the year, so in order to remain competitive in the AFC North, Baltimore brought in Arizona's Jacoby Brissett. There are several other teams to monitor as well ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. Week 9 is light on showdowns between top-tier contenders, but there are still a few contests — like the "Monday Night Football" battle featuring the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings — that will potentially reshape the title race.Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl hunt heading into Week 9.Super Bowl odds entering Week 9Odds via DraftKings, +2000 or better49ers: +580Bills: +600Bears: +780Jaguars: +950Chiefs: +1000Rams: +1100Seahawks: +1250Bengals: +1400Broncos: +1600Patriots: +1900Lions: +1900
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stock up: Jeffery Simmons trade legitimizes BearsA single move ahead of the NFL trade deadline elevated the Bears out of the pack of ordinary Super Bowl contenders and into the top tier of championship hopefuls. They suddenly own the third-shortest odds to roll through the postseason. 
While the San Francisco 49ers are still the team to beat in the NFC until proven otherwise, the Bears' momentum is even more palpable, and it is beginning to feel like the conference runs through Chicago. Monday's 34-17 win on the road over the Seattle Seahawks might have been a passing of the torch from last year's champions to the best team of 2026.Simmons unlocked all kinds of possibilities when he arrived by way of the Tennessee Titans. The three-time All-Pro defensive tackle recorded his first tackle as a Bear on the game's first play from scrimmage and earned his first sack on the following series. He dominated from start to finish and added another tackle for loss and a pass breakup in the fourth quarter. This is a new kind of weapon on the defensive front and one that gives coordinator Dennis Allen the freedom to blitz less frequently and still get pressure on the quarterback. That is an invaluable opportunity for a team that previously relied on the blitz at one of the NFL's highest rates.The only weakness on this Bears team now resides in the secondary, and Simmons' arrival should mask it to a noticeable extent. Everything else about the Bears is championship-caliber. Ben Johnson's offense might finish the year as the highest-scoring operation in the league, Caleb Williams is on an MVP trajectory, Luther Burden III is breaking out in real time and the run game remains prolific with D'Andre Swift leading the charge. Now, the defense should be capable of at least holding up its end of the deal, if not outright leading the charge in some games.
The NFC North is anyone's division. Chicago now boasts the second-best offense and second-best defense, and as a newly minted well-rounded team, that might be enough to take command and secure a top-four seed in the postseason. And with the best defensive lineman in the world and a burgeoning superstar at quarterback, the No. 1 seed is now in play, too.
        
            
                Bears assert Super Bowl candidacy: After Jeffery Simmons trade and 'MNF' win, NFC runs through Chicago
                
                    Carter Bahns                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stock down: Quarterback injuries tank Ravens' seasonYear after year, the Ravens feel the wrath of injuries at the most important position. Lamar Jackson has only played two full seasons since 2021, and the contrast in record with and without him is appalling. Now that he is slated to miss extended time with his second injury of the year — a thumb issue that requires surgery — this season is trending in the same direction as 2021, 2022 and 2025 when his absences prevented Baltimore from vying for a championship.What's more, backup Tyler Huntley is done for the season with turf toe, which leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the starter for Week 9. The trade set to bring Jacoby Brissett to town does raise the floor quite a bit, but there is no getting back to the ceiling Jackson provides.
Fagnano was the emergency third quarterback in Week 8 and was thrust into the first action of his young career when both signal-callers ahead of him departed with injuries in the first half of the loss to the Bills, and the UConn product is now tasked with keeping the offense afloat on "Thursday Night Football." The Ravens also signed Kedon Slovis off the Packers' practice squad and added Austin Reed to their own practice squad, making him the likely third quarterback against the Jaguars on "Thursday Night Football."Once Brissett arrives, it will be his show. But he was just benched in Arizona last week, so the Ravens cannot bank on him delivering enough of an upgrade over the other bleak options to keep the season alive.Ravens depth chart changesRoleWeek 8Week 9Week 10 (projected)StarterLamar JacksonJoe FagnanoJacoby BrissettBackupTyler HuntleyKedon SlovisJoe FagnanoEmergencyJoe FagnanoAustin Reed (projected)Kedon SlovisLess than one half of football entirely changed the outlook for Baltimore's season. The injuries in the opening minutes of the matchup against Buffalo relegated the Ravens from Super Bowl contention to a potential last-place finish in their own division. Their odds to win it all plummeted to +10000.Unless Jackson can recover quickly from his surgery and limit his injured reserve stint to four games or only slightly more, this will likely be a lost season. And with the potential for him to miss the rest of the year, Brissett possibly overseeing a decent offense is the only real source of optimism in Baltimore.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Long shot of the week: Steelers (+5000)The balance of power shifted immensely in the AFC North over the last week. The Ravens' quarterback injuries cleared the path forward for the other three teams, and the Steelers' head-to-head win over the Browns prompted a shakeup at the top with Pittsburgh securing sole possession of first place. After their Week 9 bye, the Steelers will have an opportunity to build separation in a second showdown with the Bengals. They beat Cincinnati in their first matchup.The reunion between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy injected new life into the offense ahead of the season, and the results are playing out on game days. The passing attack is effective even without a full-strength wide receiver room, and Jaylen Warren leads an invigorated run game that ranks third in the league in EPA per rush. And on the other side of the ball, first-year defensive coordinator Patrick Graham is easily among the best new assistant coaches in football. His unit ranks in the top eight in scoring defense (No. 3), total defense (No. 6), run defense (No. 3), third-down defense (No. 8), red-zone defense (No. 2) and takeaways (No. 3).Sunday's win over Cleveland was the greatest example yet of how everything has come together in 2026. The 27-6 triumph gave the Steelers their largest margin of victory of the season, while the six points they allowed were their fewest of the year.Week 9 games to watchBroncos at PanthersSunday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+This is a get-up-off-the-mat game for the Panthers, who lost their last two contests by a combined 38 points but were fortunate to find a one-score margin in their last outing. Bryce Young's early-season success is a thing of the past, as it seems opponents have cracked the code on stopping his breakout. The Broncos pose another stiff challenge. Denver, meanwhile, is the significantly stronger Super Bowl contender of the two and rides a four-game win streak into this cross-country trip. Sean Payton's squad is 15-0 in one-score games dating back to the middle of last season and is 5-0 in games decided by seven points or fewer this year alone. How sustainable is that? Apparently quite sustainable.Packers at PatriotsSunday, 4:25 p.m., Fox, stream on FuboThe quarterback showdown between Drake Maye and Jordan Love is the best Week 9 has to offer. Between them, there are just over 4,200 yards and 31 touchdowns on the season, and they carry identical records into their showdown. Every time the Patriots have won a game, the Packers have too. Both teams suffered their three losses in the same weeks, too. That means both are playing their best football right now with four wins in the last five weeks.Bills at VikingsMonday, 8:15 p.m., ABC, stream on Fubo
Minnesota's league-leading defense will be put to the test for the second consecutive week. Last time out, it faced the NFL's top offense and held it to 19 points. This time, it meets the second-best unit with Josh Allen coming to town. If the Vikings could limit the Lions to just two touchdowns, then they should feel confident about their ability to contain Allen and his group. The bigger question is whether Kevin O'Connell's offense can do enough to take advantage. The unit has been lifeless even in its most favorable matchups, so a banged-up Kyler Murray (hamstring) may not be entirely trustworthy against the Bills and their less-than-perfect defense.

title: Redrafting 2024 WNBA Draft: Caitlin Clark stays No. 1; where does Angel Reese land? - CBS Sports
description: The WNBA's 2024 draft class, led by Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese, has transformed the league. Their unique talents, combined with the a
body:
The WNBA's 2024 draft class, led by Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese, has transformed the league. Their unique talents, combined with the attention they demanded, made a historic new collective bargaining agreement possible and created an environment where 3.3 million people watched the Golden State Valkyries win their first title by defeating Reese and the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. When the 2024 WNBA Draft took place, the Valkyries were little more than an idea, and the league had never even played a best-of-seven series, let alone had a winner-take-all Game 7 for the title. It's almost hard to believe that Clark, Reese and the rest of the 2024 class have been in the league for three seasons now. Next year will be the final year of their rookie contracts, and Clark and Reese are eligible to sign EPIC extensions this offseason. As another long offseason begins, this is the perfect time to revisit the 2024 class with a re-draft. Clark would still go No. 1, of course, but what about Reese, Cameron Brink and French guards Carla Leite and Leila Lacan? Let's dive in. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Indiana Fever: Caitlin ClarkOriginal pick: Caitlin ClarkClark set the NCAA scoring record, led Iowa to back-to-back national championship games in her junior and senior seasons and was an international sensation long before she entered the league as the most hyped prospect ever. Regardless of which team won the 2024 Draft Lottery, Clark was going No. 1. The first three seasons of Clark's professional career have not been smooth sailing for her or the Fever, but Indiana would not hesitate to select her again. She immediately established herself as one of the WNBA's best guards with a historic rookie season, has made the All-WNBA First Team in her two healthy campaigns and is an economic engine off the court. The Fever hadn't made the playoffs for seven seasons before Clark arrived. They've made it every season since drafting her, won a franchise-record 28 games in 2026 and have become one of the most popular franchises in all of sports. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Los Angeles Sparks: Angel ReeseOriginal pick: Cameron BrinkBrink was a rim-protecting machine in college at Stanford, and her upside as a long, mobile big who could control the paint on the defensive end and space the floor on the other made her the obvious pick at No. 2 for the Sparks with the first of their two lottery selections. If the Sparks had to do it over again, though, they would choose Reese instead. Brink tore her ACL early in her rookie season and has only played 65 games as a pro. Reese, on the other hand, has grown into one of the league's best young bigs thanks in large part to her indefatigable motor. Reese fell to No. 7 despite a historic run to a national championship as a senior at LSU due to serious concerns about her offensive game, which were not unfounded. While she still needs to improve as a scorer, Reese is well on her way to being the best rebounder ever. She won Defensive Player of the Year and was instrumental in leading the Dream to the Finals. 
She has very clearly become the second-best player in this class, which no one would have predicted on draft night. The Sparks would be in a much better place right now if they had drafted Reese instead of Brink. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Chicago Sky: Carla LeiteOriginal pick: Kamilla CardosoCardoso entered the league fresh off her second national championship in three seasons with South Carolina and a dominant NCAA Tournament run as a senior. With her size, defensive ability and efficient interior scoring, it seemed like she would have a very high floor. But while her raw stats have indeed been very solid, she has not been impactful. In fact, the Sky have been slightly better with her off the floor in her first three seasons. Knowing what we know now, the pick for Chicago at No. 3 would have been Leite, who originally went No. 9 to Dallas because of her age, questions about when she would come over to the U.S. and lingering concerns in the pre-2026 CBA era about international players' willingness to prioritize the WNBA. 
Leite never even played for the Wings, who left her unprotected in the 2025 expansion draft. She then played sparingly as a rookie for the Valkyries, who also left her unprotected in the 2026 expansion draft. In Portland, she finally got a chance when Alex Sarama gave her the keys to the Fire's offense, and she had a breakout campaign that resulted in a third-place Most Improved Player finish. Leite, still only 22, is coming off one of the best high-volume pick-and-roll seasons ever, made tremendous strides as a 3-point shooter and has established herself as a franchise point guard. Even if she had followed the exact same timeline in Chicago, picking her at No. 3 would have been the right call. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Los Angeles Sparks: Leïla LacanOriginal pick: Rickea JacksonAfter the Sparks took Brink at No. 2, they waited anxiously to see what the Sky would do at No. 3. If the Sky had taken Jackson, would the Sparks really have taken both Brink and Cardoso? We'll never know, because the Sky took Cardoso, which allowed the Sparks to take Jackson at No. 4. At the time, it seemed like Los Angeles had added the best big and the best wing in the class. 
Jackson never seemed to mesh with then-Sparks coach Lynne Roberts, however, and despite putting up some big scoring numbers, was traded to the Sky last offseason for Ariel Atkins. Four games into her Sky tenure, Jackson tore her ACL; she missed the remainder of last season and her status for 2027 is unclear. If the Sparks could do it over again, Lacan would be the pick. Like Leite, Lacan fell to No. 10 because she was a young French guard, and she didn't make her WNBA debut until 2025. But since she's arrived, she's been extremely impactful, especially on the defensive end, where she's already one of the best perimeter defenders in the league. In her two seasons, the Sun were 18-35 with Lacan and 4-31 without her as she has, indeed, missed extensive time due to international commitments.There would certainly be spacing concerns with Reese and Lacan, who is an inconsistent shooter, but the defensive potential would be off the charts. Ironically, the Sparks' major issues on that side of the ball are a big reason they still haven't made the playoffs since 2020. Lacan is also still only 22 and has more room to grow than most other players in this class. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Dallas Wings: Cameron BrinkOriginal pick: Jacy SheldonHeading into the 2024 draft, the Wings were coming off a semifinals appearance and had a crowded frontcourt, which is why they took Sheldon over some of the bigs still on the board, including Reese. Sheldon had played five seasons at Ohio State, was an elite perimeter defender at the collegiate level and a reliable 3-point shooter. The logic behind the selection made sense; she could come in and fill some needs right away for a team that expected to be in the playoff hunt again. As we know now, none of that happened. Sheldon struggled and was traded to the Sun after her rookie season, and the Wings were a disaster in 2024 (and 2025). Despite their frontcourt logjam at the time, and what has happened to Brink early in her professional career, she would be the pick here at No. 5 if she were still on the board. 
The defense is very real when Brink can stay on the floor, and it's almost impossible to find players who can protect the rim as well as she can while also being mobile enough to not get exposed away from the basket.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Washington Mystics: Rickea JacksonOriginal pick: Aaliyah EdwardsAt the time, Edwards was the obvious pick at No. 7 for a Mystics team that had learned in February it would be without Elena Delle Donne indefinitely (she never played another game for the franchise). Edwards was a standout for UConn, which always produces pro-ready players, and her mobility at her size was enticing. Edwards only lasted one season in D.C. before being traded to the Sun for Sheldon, whom the Mystics later flipped to the Sky for Chicago's 2028 first-round pick. If they could guarantee that chain of events would happen again, maybe Edwards would still be the choice given the value of the Sky's 2028 first-rounder.
But if Jackson was still on the board at No. 7, it would be hard to pass her up, even knowing about her eventual ACL tear. Jackson remains the best wing in this class, and her ability to create her own offense is exactly the type of skill set the Mystics have been missing in recent seasons. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Chicago Sky: Sydney TaylorOriginal pick: Angel ReeseThe Sky traded up from No. 8 to No. 7 because they desperately wanted Reese. At the time, there were real questions about their decision to take Cardoso and Reese, which proved to be a mistake. The real issue, though, was taking Cardoso at No. 3 instead of a perimeter player, and getting Reese at No. 7 was tremendous value. Reese would obviously not be on the board for the Sky's second pick in this redraft scenario, so instead they would take Taylor, who is actually on the roster. After going undrafted in 2024 out of UMass and Louisville, Taylor spent a few years playing in Lithuania and Poland. She earned a training camp invite from the Sky ahead of the 2026 season and ended up making the final roster. 
Taylor ended up playing a big role after Jackson and Skylar Diggins went down with injuries. She was one of the few bright spots for the Sky during another disappointing campaign. She's extremely quick and an elite finisher at the basket, and earned a spot on the All-Rookie Team. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Minnesota Lynx: Aaliyah EdwardsOriginal pick: Alissa PiliThe Lynx moved down from No. 8 to No. 7 and got a 2026 first-round pick swap for their trouble, which they eventually used to select 2026 unanimous Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles. It's fair to wonder if they would have won the title in 2024 if they had just stayed at No. 7 and taken Reese, but it's hard to find too much fault in a process that led to Miles. It is easy to criticize Cheryl Reeve's decision to select Pili, who never seemed like a WNBA player. She lasted less than two seasons before being waived and has only played 46 career games. There's no chance the Lynx would select Pili again. Edwards is the pick instead because she would have been a better fit for the Lynx's system than the paint-bound Cardoso. While she's never lived up to her full potential, she finally found her stride in Connecticut last season. Could she have done so sooner in Minnesota? Reeve's ability to develop players and put them in positions to succeed suggests the answer is yes. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Dallas Wings: Isobel BorlaseOriginal pick: Carla LeiteThe Wings went draft-and-stash with their second first-round selection in 2024 and nailed the pick. The only problem was they left Leite unprotected in the Valkyries' expansion draft, and she never even played for the team. Leite would be unavailable in a re-draft, but another draft-and-stash player would make sense for the Wings here: Borlase. The Australian didn't arrive in the WNBA until 2026, after she had won MVP of the WNBL in her native country. Very few rookies earn more playing time in the playoffs than in the regular season, but that's just what Borlase did for the Dream in their run to the Finals. She never once looked scared and was one of the few players who could get anything going in the team's Game 7 defeat to the Valkyries. Borlase has a bright future and would be a great fit on this current Wings roster.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Connecticut Sun: Emma ČechováOriginal pick: Leïla LacanThe 2024 Sun were a title contender and only rostered 11 players due to salary cap concerns, which made Lacan a perfect option as a draft-and-stash candidate. That turned out to be a brilliant pick, but Lacan would not be available at No. 10 in a re-draft.  But given the Sun's roster and cap crunch, they still would have looked for a draft-and-stash player. In that case, Čechová, who we're including in this class because she was eligible for the draft starting in 2024, makes the most sense. Čechová signed with the Lynx last season as an undrafted free agent and was off to an excellent start before tearing her ACL. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. New York Liberty: Kamilla CardosoOriginal pick: Marquesha DavisAfter losing in the Finals in 2023, the Liberty took a big upside swing on Davis with their late first-round pick in 2024. The Liberty ended up winning the title in 2024 and got nothing along the way from Davis, who only played 29 games with the club before being waived. She is now out of the league. Cardoso is not a good fit for the Liberty's style -- then or now -- but it would be impossible to pass on her at this point in the draft. And if the Liberty didn't want to add Cardoso, they easily could have traded the pick if she was still on the board at No. 11. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Atlanta Dream: Jacy SheldonOriginal pick: Nyadiew PuochThe options were pretty limited at this point in the draft, and the Dream understandably went for upside with Puoch, a.k.a., "The Block Doctor." She never ended up playing for Atlanta, but was selected by Portland in the expansion draft and had a nice close to the 2026 season. But if given a redo, the Dream would select Sheldon. The feisty point guard has played for four teams in three seasons, and really struggled in Chicago last season. It's still possible she could become a useful defensive-minded bench guard, especially if she can ever find some stability.

title: Biggest MLB offseason questions: How long will lockout last? Will we see a free agency frenzy? - CBS Sports
description: The 2026 World Series is in the rearview and it's time for the winter to get underway -- until a likely lockout g
body:
The 2026 World Series is in the rearview and it's time for the winter to get underway -- until a likely lockout gets in the way
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:47 am ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Not so long ago, the Milwaukee Brewers were crowned World Series champions, and at the moment of the last out, the 2026-27 Major League offseason began. So let's talk about that. The winter ahead is one shot through with uncertainty, as labor strife figures to roil the sport and perhaps even compromise the 2027 season. Those matters, vital as they are, won't be the only story, and we'll still have the familiar presences of free agency and trade talk to sustain us. To set the scene for all that's ahead in advance of the 2027 campaign – good, ill, or somewhere in the middle – we're here to take a look at the five questions that will inform an offseason that's going to be quite unusual and – for good, ill, or somewhere in the middle – probably unforgettable. Let's explore those five queries right now … 1. How long will the lockout last?The current collective bargaining agreement – or CBA, the accord that governs the working relationship between clubs/owners and players – is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1 of this year. At that time, MLB owners are all but certain to lock out the players. That's a labor stoppage, and that means the offseason will be brought to a sudden halt. The lockout, the purpose of which is to preempt a players' strike, will last until a new CBA is agreed to. Agreeing to a new CBA will be no simple matter, and owners and their hireling, commissioner Rob Manfred, are pushing for a cap on team payrolls. The players, as represented by their union, the MLBPA, have never shown any willingness to agree to a cap-and-floor system. There are a lot of other issues to iron out, as the CBA is an all-encompassing document, but the fight over a cap will be what drags out the lockout.

        
            
                MLB CBA negotiations timeline: League proposes delaying salary cap for 'smoother transition'
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The heart of the matter is whether the lockout will last long enough to push back, abbreviate, or – perish the thought – cancel entirely the 2027 season. The latter is the worst-case scenario and is highly unlikely, but it's a possibility, however remote. More of a threat is a 2027 season that doesn't span the usual 162 games. We have a recent precedent to guide us. The last time the CBA was up for negotiation during the offseason of 2021-22, owners locked out the players for 99 days. That meant a shortened spring training by about two and a half weeks and forced the regular season calendar to be compressed, albeit while still preserving the 162-game docket. As such, we can say that if the lockout lasts beyond the middle of March 2027, then we'll likely lose regular-season games. For further context, here's a brief history of modern labor stoppages in the sport: 
MLB work stoppageDates1972 strikeApril 1-13, 19721973 lockoutFeb. 8-25, 1973 1976 lockoutMarch 1-17, 19761980 strikeApril 1-8, 19801981 strikeJune 12 - July 31, 19811985 strikeAug. 6-7, 19851990 lockoutFeb. 15 - March 18, 19901994-95 strikeAug. 12, 1994 - March 31, 19952021-22 lockoutDec. 2, 2021 - March 10, 2022Just two, the 1981 and 1994-95 player strikes, significantly compromised seasons. The 1994-95 stoppage cost us the 1994 World Series, and it took years for the sport to recover from the resulting fan disaffection. As for the 2027 season, the worst-case scenario may not be the loss of the entire season but rather the loss of 60 games off the regular-season slate. Here's the explanation from our recent Lockout 101 piece: "… [I]f the lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That matters because Manfred and the league hope to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation in 2028. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that new media rights structure. This amounts to a major incentive, at least on the league side, to agree to a new CBA before June arrives."Obviously, the hope is that the lockout doesn't even affect the spring training calendar, let alone cost us a major chunk of the regular season.
        
            
                Why MLB could see an early free agency frenzy before the potential Dec. 1 lockout
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
2. What will the next CBA look like?As noted, the big fight is over whether or not MLB will have a cap-and-floor structure moving forward, as is the case in the NFL, NBA, and NHL. Owners have tied every single proposal wrinkle to date to the players' acceptance of a cap. However, it remains highly unlikely, at least until further notice, that the union would ever agree to such a thing. The other major issue is a likely restructuring of the revenue-sharing system. Specifically, the next CBA is highly likely to revise the system so that local broadcast revenues are shared much more evenly. Fortunately, there's already some common ground on this issue, and a reordering of that system would directly address the revenue disparities within MLB that are such a reliable source of consternation – and misinformation – without the grievous labor war that a continued cap push would force upon us.  Otherwise, some other key wrinkles and changes may come out of the wash. That list potentially includes: Further expansion of the postseason, possibly from 12 to 14 teams;A roadmap for league expansion before the end of the decade, likely from 30 to 32 franchises;The reduction of the regular season from 162 games to 154 games;The implementation of an international draft;Changes to the Competitive Balance Tax, or "Luxury Tax," as it's informally and more accurately known, in the event a cap isn't agreed to;Structural changes to the MLB Draft;Structural changes to free agency and salary arbitration.This doesn't get into evergreen matters like an increase in the minimum salary, draft bonus pools, the qualifying offer system, active roster sizes, and so forth. There's a lot to sort out, to say the least. The expectation is that the next CBA is going to lead to sweeping changes to the sport starting in 2027 and, perhaps by design, growing over time. Even if there's no cap and floor, the economic structure of MLB is almost certain to look very different after this winter. 3. Where -- and when -- will Tarik Skubal and other major free agents sign?Overall, this is one of the weakest free agent classes in living memory, but there is elite superstar value to be found at the tip-top with back-to-back (for the moment) American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. Skubal, who turns 30 on Nov. 20, remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and he's going to be paid like it. The expectation is that he'll wind up signing the largest pitcher contract in MLB history and perhaps also fetch the highest-ever annual salary for a pitcher. It's not out of the question that Skubal's next contract could approach or even surpass $400 million in total value. At those rates, the incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers and the free-spending New York Mets are the consensus favorites. The Chicago Cubs are also reportedly heavily interested in Skubal, and surprise bidders are always possible. Other notable free agent names include Freddy Peralta, Michael King, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trevor Rogers, Adrian Morejon, and Teruaki Sato. Our ranking of the top 50 2026-27 free agents has you covered.
        
            
                Ranking the top 50 MLB free agents for the 2026-27 offseason, plus landing spots for every player
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The "when" of all this is more complicated thanks to the upcoming lockout detailed above. Will premium free agents and their representatives rush to find some stability in advance of the stoppage, during which no major-league transactions will be permitted, or will they decide that the long game will be better for their markets? It's possible that the biggest spenders on the team side will look to make moves early, as the barrel of the next CBA figures to be leveled directly at them and their abundant revenues. Or maybe the unknown will have a chilling effect on spending before we arrive at the lockout. The past is not always prelude, but let's note that we saw a flurry of spending leading up to the lockout of 2021-22. Indeed, in November 2021, MLB teams committed more than $1.7 billion to free agents prior to the lockout. The Texas Rangers alone guaranteed $500 million to a new middle infield – Corey Seager and Marcus Semien – before the lockout put an end to such things. In all, teams put ink to paper on five nine-figure contracts prior to the 2021-22 lockout. The comparisons may not entirely hold since this upcoming CBA should bring about a much more drastic re-ordering of the sport than the current expiring CBA did. As such, teams may proceed cautiously given all the uncertainties. Or, as just mentioned, they may seek to get business done before the ways of doing business change entirely. We'll see soon enough. If we do see the dollars start flying before the lockout, then the upcoming Nov. 10-12 general managers meetings in Las Vegas may occasion the groundwork for all those deals. 4. Any blockbuster trades on the way?Will a lackluster free agent class mean more headline-grabbing trades? That may indeed be answered in the affirmative this winter. Yes, the CBA uncertainty will have a bearing on trades, especially those that involve the assumption of major salary obligations, but big trades still figure to be a prominent part of this offseason. It's of course impossible to know who's going to be dealt ahead of time, but some big names perhaps on the move this winter include Francisco Lindor, Mason Miller, Spencer Strider, Hunter Greene, Otto Lopez, Jeremy Peña, Ketel Marte, Jacob deGrom, and of course others. Paul Skenes? Almost certainly not, but you'll just as certainly hear his name bandied about.
        
            
                Top 25 MLB trade candidates for 2026-27 offseason: Paul Skenes, Jeremy Peña and more who could move
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Turning back to last lockout, it was mostly minor trades before the sport shut down. Yes, we'll see big ones this time around, but they may not happen until we have a new CBA in place and the lockout is over. 5. Who will get the No. 1 overall draft pick? Let's make time for the losers, shall we? The teams that didn't make the postseason in 2026 and otherwise qualify will take part in the draft lottery, which is presently scheduled for Dec. 8. That lottery will determine which teams get the top six picks in the 2027 MLB Draft. This year, 16 of the 18 non-playoff teams will be in the lottery. Non-playoff teams can be barred from the lottery if they've had lottery picks in two consecutive seasons. If a team is a revenue-sharing payor, then it can't be in the lottery in consecutive years. Those wrinkles this year mean that the San Francisco Giants and Pittsburgh Pirates will not be in the lottery and can't pick higher than 10th in the 2027 Draft. Here's how the preliminary lottery odds look for those 16 teams in the mix, based on how they finished the 2026 season: TeamOdds of getting No. 1 overall pickOdds of getting lottery pick (top six)Rockies19.1%87.6%Angels19.1%87.6%Athletics19.1%87.6%Royals11.57%73.0%Mets8.68%62.6%Reds6.37%51.1%Tigers4.51%39.2%Mariners3.13%28.7%Nationals2.08%19.9%Twins1.62%15.7%Cardinals1.27%12.5%Blue Jays1.04%10.3%Orioles0.93%9.3%Marlins0.69%6.9%Rangers0.58%5.8%Diamondbacks0.23%2.3%It's too soon to know which players will be in the mix for that top pick since the amateur seasons haven't begun yet. However, two early favorites to go No. 1 are University of Florida shortstop Brendan Lawson and Mississippi State left-hander Tomas Valinicius.

body:
The 2026 NFL season is at the halfway point, Week 9, so that means some of the top players who have dealt with long-term injuries are ready to begin their returns to action. Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Micah Parsons' 21-day practice window to return from the torn ACL and torn meniscus is now open. That means Parsons will begin practicing with the Packers for the first time this season, with the goal of returning for the Thanksgiving week game against the Los Angeles Rams."He put a lot of effort and work into this. Having him out there will be a big boost for our team," LaFleur said, via ESPN.LaFleur also indicated Parsons will begin practicing as a limited participant in individual position drills while ramping him up to be full throttle in a couple of weeks. 
The New Orleans Saints could also get a key piece of theirs back as well: 2026 eighth overall pick wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. The rookie out of Arizona State dealt with hamstring issues in college, which have delayed his NFL debut. However, New Orleans Football Network reported Tyson will return to practice.While that is positive news for the Packers and Saints, many injury situations aren't as optimistic in Week 9. The Rams got bad news on Jaylen Watson on Wednesday, with the cornerback requiring season-ending shoulder surgery. He missed a game earlier this year after dislocating the shoulder and reaggravated the injury in last week's game against the Chargers.
"That's a big blow ... He's been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, but just kind of understanding the totality of it all, it was recommended for him to get that surgery, and he'll be on IR," coach Sean McVay said.Odds courtesy of DraftKings SportsbookJacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens (+10)Jaguars: RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) QUESTIONABLERavens: SAF Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), QB Lamar Jackson (right thumb), QB Tyler Huntley (toe) OUT; RB Adam Randall (neck), CB Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) QUESTIONABLEBhayshul Tuten suffered an ankle injury last week and played through it. He is officially questionable after not practicing all week. Chris Rodriguez would likely see more touches if Tuten is ruled out or limited in any way. DE Travon Walker (rib) is also questionable and was limited on Tuesday and Wednesday after not practicing on Monday.The Ravens got their starting quarterback Lamar Jackson back last week, but the return was short-lived. Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the first play and was quickly ruled out. Backup Tyler Huntley then suffered a turf toe injury that will sideline him for the rest of the season, per ESPN. Both head to injured reserve. Joe Fagnano, the emergency third quarterback last week who came in after the first two were ruled out, will be at the helm for Baltimore, marking his first NFL start. He was a full participant the last two days of practice after being limited on Monday. Trey Hendrickson was limited on Monday and was a full participant on Tuesday and Wednesday. Adam Randall (neck) and CB Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) are both questionable. 
Cincinnati Bengals at Atlanta Falcons (+3)The Bengals didn't practice on Wednesday, and the Falcons held a walkthrough, so their injury reports are estimations of practice participation.On the Bengals side, four players did not participate: DT Jonathan Allen (NIR/Rest), S Kyle Dugger (quad), DE Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) and CB DJ Turner II (heel). The only other player listed on the report was S Jordan Battle (hamstring), who was estimated as limited.The Falcons, on the other hand, had only one non-participant: WR Zachariah Branch. Their limited players included LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), as well as LB Devine Diablo (forearm) and RB Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring), who both missed last week's game. De Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip) and DE James Pearce Jr. (NIR/other) were all full participants. 
New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs (-10)Jets WR Garrett Wilson is in concussion protocol and did not practice, while RB Breece Hall could make a return after missing multiple games. Hall (quad), edge David Bailey (groin), edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) and TE Mason Taylor were all limited in Wednesday's practice, and coach Aaron Glenn said they are "trending in the right direction." One Chiefs player did not practice on Wednesday: DL Peter Woods (neck). Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) and WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) were both limited. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee), LB Nick Bolton (neck) and LB Drye Tranquill (pectoral) were all full participants. Limited players included CB Mansoor Delane, DT Omarr Norman-Lott and WR Nikko Remigio.Detroit Lions at Miami Dolphins (+7)Safety Kerby Joseph will be out for the Lions, coach Dan Campbell said. Detroit's non-participants for Wednesday's practice were: LB Jack Campbell, who remains in the hospital after suffering a scary injury last week, C Cade Mays (ankle), CB D.J. Reed (hip) and EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion). WR Amon-Ra St. Brown was limited with a rib injury. S Kerby Joseph (knee), LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) and RB Jacob Saylors (neck) were also limited and CB Rock Ya-Sin (cramps) was the one player listed as a full participant in the estimation of their walkthrough.
The Dolphins had a long injury report this week, with eight players limited, including LS Tucker Addington, RB Kaytron Allen, EDGE Malik Herring, TE Will Kacmarek, EDGE Chop Robinson, DL Zach Sieler, S Michael Taaffe and S Dante Trader Jr. Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5)The Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols, DT Daron Payne, and DT Javon Kinlaw on IR, meaning they will miss at least four games each. Quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow) was a full participant. WR Treylon Burks (foot) and WR Stefon Diggs (NIR/rest) were the two Commanders players who did not practice on Wednesday. TE John Bates (shoulder), G Sam Cosmi (knee) and DT Shy Tuttle (shoulder) were all limited. DT Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) and TE Colson Yankoff were full participants.The biggest news is that CB Jaylen Watson needs season-ending shoulder surgery. The Rams opened LB Myles Garrett's 21-day practice window this week and he is on track to practice this week. Garrett suffered a knee injury in the season opener and has not practiced since, but was a limited participant on Wednesday. CB Trent McDuffie came in "feeling better than expected," per coach Sean McVay. McDuffie did not practice, along with LS Joe Cardona, S Kam Curl and TE Colby Parkinson. G Steve Avila, TE Terrance Ferguson, LB Grant Stuard and WR Jordan Whittington were all limited. QB Matthew Stafford appeared on the injury report, but was a full participant. 
Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers (+2.5)Wide receiver Pat Bryant was designated for return from injured reserve on Wednesday and was a full participant. WR Jaylen Waddle (chest) was also a full participant. DL Zach Allen (NIR/rest) and WR Courtland Sutton (NIR/rest) were the team's limited participants. Four players did not practice Wednesday: S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), S Brandon Jones (hamstring), DL Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) and CB Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle).The Panthers' Wednesday injury report is an approximation. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant. Linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), LG Damien Lewis (knee), LB Bobby Okereke (foot) and CB Will Lee III (hamstring). Phillips and Lewis both missed last week's game. LB Corey Bullock (quadriceps) and LB Torricelli Simpkins III (ankle) were listed as limited participants. DT Bobby Brown III (hand) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring).Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis Colts (+5.5)The Dallas Cowboys had an extensive number of players who didn't practice on Wednesday: DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle), TE Jake Ferguson (ankle), OT Broderick Jones (vet rest day), edge rusher Malachi Lawrence (ankle), S P.J. Locke III (concussion), Von Miller (vet rest day) and WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs). Both Downs and Locke worked off to the side. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Lawrence will be out for multiple weeks, and that Dallas is weighing the possibility of putting him on injured reserve. 
Four players were limited: WR George Pickens (limited), TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin), G Tyler Smith (ankle) and LB Dee Winters (calf). Five Indianapolis Colts didn't practice on Wednesday: WR Keenan Allen (vet rest day), LB Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee), TE Andrew Ogletree (knee), CB Justin Walley (knee) and CB Charvarius Ward (vet rest day). Running back Jonathan Taylor (vet rest day) was the only Colt with limited practice participation. New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5)Two notable Giants players sidelined during Wednesday's practice were OLB Abdul Carter (illness) and RB Cam Skattebo (hamstring). Limited players include: OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), LB Malik Harrison (groin), CB Colton Hood (illness), WR Charlie Jones (hand) and OT Andrew Thomas (groin). Tight end Theo Johnson (neck), OT Marcus Mbow (knee) and DL DJ Reader (knee) were all on the report, but able to practice as full participants.
The Eagles' season isn't letting up on the injury front, with another long list this week. Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) and WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who have both missed time this year, were both non-participants. The offense is already without QB Jalen Hurts and without their stars in the run and pass game, their struggles only intensify. LB Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), DB Michael Carter (abdomen), WR Britain Covey (knee), CB Jonathan Jones (hamstring) and WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were also sidelined for Wednesday's practice. K Jake Elliott (right Ankle), OLB Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and OLB Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) were their limited participants. The full participants included: LB Zack Baun (shoulder), T Markel Bell (finger), DT Jordan Davis (thumb), G Landon Dickerson (hip), TE Dallas Goedert (knee), QB Tanner McKee (chest), DB Kenny Moore (glute) and DT Moro Ojomo (neck).Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-3)Browns QB Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol, and he did not practice on Wednesday. Also sidelined were LB Quincy Williams (hamstring), T Austin Barber (calf) and DT Maliek Collins (elbow). WR Denzel Boston (calf), CB Myles Harden (hamstring), C/G Elgton Jenkins (knee), LB Carson Schwesinger (wrist/ankle) and DE Jared Verse were all limited.RB Alvin Kamara (NIR/rest) was the only Saints player who did not participate. WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring), OT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle), RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion), CB Martin Emerson (shin) and OT Asim Richards (thumb) were all limited. S Justin Reid (concussion), G Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DE Nathan Shepherd (illness) were all full participants. 
Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10)The Raiders had a short injury report on Wednesday. CB Darien Porter (groin) was the only Raiders player who was a non-participant, while DT Thomas Booker (ankle), DT Foley Fatukasi (shoulder/elbow) and TE Ian Thomas (ankle) were all limited.The 49ers have been dealing with significant injuries all season and had some big names on their injury report again this week. DE Nick Bosa (knee/calf) and WR Christian Kirk were limited, while WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and RB Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) did not practice. Evans and Samuel were both sidelined last week. LB Luke Giggord, CB Nate Hobbs, WR Demarcus Robinson, CB Upton Stout and LB Garrett Wallow were all limited. Among those who didn't practice were T Trent Williams and DB Siran Neal.Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5)DeMeco Ryans said Monday he had "no significant update" on RB David Montgomery (groin), who missed two games ahead of the bye. He was one of two Texans who did not practice on Wednesday, joined by S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand). LB Azeez Al-Shaair 9groin), TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot) and T Braden Smith (ankle) were the team's limited participants, while T Blake Fisher (thumb) and S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) were full participants.The Chargers had four players not participate in Wednesday's practice: CB Deane Leonard (concussion), DE Khalil Mack (NIR/rest), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and S Kendall Williamson (calf). Seven players were limited, including TE David Njoku (fibula), G Kayode Awosika (fibula), CB Donte Jackson, CB Rodney Shelley and LB Denzel Perryman. The Chargers are still looking for their first win of the season.Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-8.5)Seahawks QB Sam Darnold is out this week after suffering a quad injury in last week's game. Drew Lock will start in his place. The Seahawks did not report any injuries on Wednesday before press time. This article will be updated.QB Jacoby Brissett, who is finalizing a trade to the Ravens, did not participate in Wednesday's practice. S Budda Baker, C Hjalte Froddolt, G Jon Gaines, RB Bam Knight, G Isaac Seumalo, LB Josh Sweat and T Jayden Williams were all absent as well. G Isaiah Adams, DT Walker Nolen and WR Michael Wilson were all limited, while WR Reggie Virgil was a full participant.Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3)EDGE Micah Parsons returned to practice as a limited participant after the team opened his 21-day practice window. G Aaron Banks (knee), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), CB Keisean Nixon (groin) and WR Christian Watson were also limited participants. LB Zaire Franklin (shin), G/T Travis Glover (knee) and TE Josh Whyle (concussion) did not participate.The bad news on WR A.J. Brown continues, as he was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice with an ankle/knee injury that sidelined him last week. DT Christian Barmore (illness) and TE Hunter Henry (foot) were other notable players absent. QB Drake Maye was on the injury report with a right shoulder, but was a full participant. S Kevin Byard III (chest), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), WR Mack Hollins (calf), OLB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder/knee), OT Morgan Moses (foot) and OL Greg Van Roten were all limited, as the team's injuries continue to pile.Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6)Baker Mayfield was on the injury report with a right thumb, which caused him to miss multiple games, but he was a full participant. Three Bucs players did not practice on Wednesday: OLB Yaya Diaby (knee), WR Emeka Egbuka (foot) and DL Elijah Roberts (personal). This article will be updated.Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings (+3.5)The Bills and Vikings will release their initial injury reports on Thursday, three days before kickoff on Monday Night Football.

        As remarkable as it sounds, we've reached the midway point of the 2026 regular season now that Week 9 is on our doorstep. The first half of the year has heard underdogs bark loudly, and there's no reason to think that'll subside as we barrel down this second leg of the season. That's especially true this week as there are eight home underdogs on the Week 9 slate. Normally, this is a recipe for the league to flip on its head, particularly after a Week 8 schedule that was mostly chalk. Last week, we correctly identified the Raiders as a live road underdog as they came out with the outright win over the Jets, but favorites largely owned the rest of the schedule. Water may find its level in Week 9, however, which is why we have three road favorites firmly on upset alert as we look forward to another week in the NFL. All lines via DraftKings; All times ETGreen Bay Packers (+3) at New England PatriotsWhen: 4:25 p.m. ET | Where: Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, Massachusetts)TV: Fox | Stream: (Fubo, try for free)Packers ML odds: +142Green Bay and New England have sort of mirrored each other to this point in the season. They both started the year 1-2 and have since surged back into playoff contention with 4-1 records over the past five weeks. Jordan Love leads the NFL in passing yards entering Week 8, while Drake Maye leads the league in total yards and touchdowns from Weeks 4-8. So, both of these teams are quite hot heading into this Week 9 matchup in Foxborough. 
That said, injuries have plagued the Patriots offense, with wideout A.J. Brown missing Week 8 with a knee injury and tight end Hunter Henry leaving last week's win over Miami with a foot injury. Those are two pivotal outlets for Maye in the passing game that he may not have when he goes up against an emerging Packers defense. Over the last five games, the Packers have given up 14.6 points per game, which ranks third in the NFL. With a potentially limited cast around Maye, Green Bay's strength could end up winning the day and the game. Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings (+3.5)When: Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET | Where: U.S. Bank Stadium (Minneapolis)TV: ESPN | Stream: (Fubo, try for free)Vikings ML odds: +150Most of the attention for this game will go to the best-on-best matchup between the Bills offense and the Vikings defense. After all, Buffalo is averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game entering Week 9, while Minnesota is holding opponents to a league-low 13.3 points per game. Something will need to give there, and it could be the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense that has the advantage. 
Coming into Week 9, Minnesota leads the NFL with a 69.1% blitz rate. Against the blitz this season, Allen ranks 20th among 31 qualified quarterbacks in passer rating (88.2) and is tied for the second-most interceptions (3). Of course, Allen's rushing ability can help negate Minnesota's pass rush, but his passing numbers against the blitz are noteworthy. Meanwhile, this could be a solid spot for Minnesota's offense to find its footing. Kyler Murray hasn't been as dynamic under center as the Vikings hoped when they acquired him this offseason, and the team has largely won in spite of the offense. That said, Buffalo's defense is allowing 25.9 points per game this season, which is tied for 24th in the NFL entering Week 9. Playing in one of the better home-field environments also helps Minnesota's chances. Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5)When: 4:05 p.m. ET | Where: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Chargers ML odds: +180The Chargers have to win a game at some point, right? Right?! So far, nothing has worked for Los Angeles, as it is 0-7 this season and ranks last in the NFL in points per game (14.1) while leading the league in turnovers (17). The Chargers also haven't scored a touchdown since the third quarter of Week 5. It's been an unmitigated disaster. 
While it's hard to imagine the tide turning, there's at least a glimmer of hope this week against a surprisingly shaky Texans defense. Maybe the bye week was enough for them to take a breather and get right, but what we've seen on the field so far hasn't been anything like what they were in 2025. The Texans have allowed 30-plus points three times this season after doing so once last year. They've also had three 300-yard passing games allowed, after none in 2025. Texans defensive ranks20252026PPG2nd18thYPG1st19INTT-3rdT-24thIf they continue to look sluggish defensively, maybe the Texans open the door for the Chargers to catch lightning in a bottle at home. Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers (+2.5)When: 1 p.m. ET | Where: Bank of America Stadium (Charlotte)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Panthers ML odds: +124Under Dave Canales (since 2024), the Panthers are a respectable 8-9 as a home underdog (11-6 ATS). If you cut it to the start of last season, Carolina is 6-4 as a home underdog, so this is not only a spot it is familiar with, but it's also come out on top with straight-up wins more often than one would think. Yes, this matchup against Denver comes at a bad time for Bryce Young and the offensive line. Carolina's offensive line is banged up, which has led to Bryce Young enduring 11 sacks over the past two games. With the Broncos tied for the fourth-most sacks (23) in the NFL through Week 8, this, on paper, has the possibility of getting ugly. That said, I wonder if the Panthers continue to find success as an overlooked team at home, especially having the rest advantage after playing last Thursday. Meanwhile, don't sleep on Denver having a bit of a letdown in Week 9 after pulling off a marquee win over the Chiefs last Sunday. Cincinnati Bengals at Atlanta Falcons (+3)When: 9:30 a.m. ET | Where: Santiago Bernabéu (Madrid, Spain)TV: NFL Network Falcons ML odds: +142The NFL heads back out into international waters as the Bengals and Falcons square off in Madrid.After watching both of these offenses last week, it's hard to see the Falcons keeping pace with the Bengals. That said, lost in Joe Burrow's six-touchdown performance was that Tennessee dropped 36 points against Cincinnati's defense. Cam Ward, who has had an up-and-down start to his career, threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 41 yards against a Bengals defense that is starting to get dinged up. The Bengals lost Cashius Howell (fractured wrist), corner DJ Turner (heel), and defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle), all of whom suffered injuries against the Titans. Turner and Johnson could play this week, but the unit isn't 100%. As for the Falcons, they are getting a boost defensively as top edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is back after serving his eight-game suspension to begin the year. Cincinnati is also giving up 4.8 yards per rush this season, which is tied for the fourth-highest in the NFL. That suggests Bijan Robinson could dazzle on the international stage, especially after seeing Tony Pollard total 117 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns against the Bengals last week. If it's a ground-controlled game for Atlanta, that could be the avenue to pulling off the win.

title: Why Ravens should trade Derrick Henry: Don't let Baltimore's QB woes drag down 'King Henry' - CBS Sports
description: The running back should have a chance to win his elusive crown before it's too late
body:
The running back should have a chance to win his elusive crown before it's too late
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:10 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches, several notable players are on the trade bubble. One notable player who should also be in discussion is Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Henry, 32, is a future Hall of Famer in the middle of his 11th season in the NFL and third season with the Ravens. Through eight games, Henry has rushed for 632 yards and eight touchdowns and has carried the ball a league-high 158 times. His 4.0 yards per carry this season is nearly a full yard lower than his career average. Henry started the season with a bang. He had 144 yards and three touchdowns in Baltimore's season-opener and scored eight touchdowns in the season's first five games. His production has tapered off since, though. Henry (who has just one other 100-yard rushing performance this season) has averaged just 52 rushing yards over Baltimore's past three games and has scored just one touchdown over the past month. 
Below are the three reasons why Baltimore should consider trading Henry sometime over the next week. 
Baltimore's current situation While they are an even 4-4 through eight games, the Ravens' season is, for all intents and purposes, over, unless Jacoby Brissett can save Baltimore's sinking ship. After a 4-1 start, the Ravens have lost three straight games to fall to last place in the AFC North division. Lamar Jackson (right thumb injury) might miss the rest of the season, and backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) will be out for the remainder of the campaign. Those injuries have compelled the Ravens to trade for Brissett, who was recently demoted to third string in Arizona. Baltimore's decision to trade for Brissett is a clear indication that the Ravens don't intend to throw the white flag. While that is admirable, Baltimore would be better served making decisions now that can improve their team in the long term. 
Unless Brissett plays at a Pro Bowl level, the Ravens aren't going anywhere this season. They were a solid team with Jackson, an average team with Huntley and are now a substandard team with Brissett. That's the same Brissett who was benched this past Sunday after going 10-of-23 (with an interception) against a Cowboys defense that has been one of the league's worst this season. Baltimore has been outscored a combined 71-23 over its last two games. The offensive line is substandard, and the defense has struggled to stop anyone in the red zone. The issues in Baltimore go well beyond the quarterback. Looking at their remaining schedule, the Ravens' Week 10 home game against the winless Chargers is the only game where Baltimore would be a betting favorite. There's a chance that Brissett can help the Ravens claw to eight or nine wins, but unless Jackson is able to make a late-season return, the odds of Baltimore making the playoffs — and doing anything if they get there — are slim to none. 
What the Ravens could get in return for HenryBaltimore would undoubtedly get a decent return for Henry, whose name alone is worth a second-round pick. Several playoff-contending teams would surely be interested in acquiring a running back of Henry's caliber for the stretch run. The Giants and Vikings are among the teams most likely to be interested in acquiring Henry. The Bengals might be, too, but it's unlikely that Baltimore would trade Henry to a division rival. New York is especially interesting. Would the Ravens facilitate a trade that would reunite Henry with their former coach, John Harbaugh? One would think that they would if the Giants made them the right offer. 
As noted above, Henry's name alone is worth a second-round pick. At this point, it's a pretty open market for running backs who might be available. The Colts' Jonathan Taylor tops that list, with Tennessee's Tony Pollard coming in behind him. Taylor would be the top running back available regardless of Henry's status. Taylor is significantly younger and has been more productive in recent weeks (although he was barely used during the Colts' recent loss to the Jaguars). But because there are multiple teams that could use help at running back, whoever loses out on getting Taylor (assuming the Colts trade him) would surely try to get Henry if he is available. As far as a trade is concerned, it only takes one team to drive up the price. If a bidding war is created, it's possible the Ravens could even get more than a second-round pick for Henry. And while a first-round pick might be a stretch, anything is possible, which is why the Ravens should at least explore the possibility of moving Henry, whose trade value will probably never be higher than it is now. 
Help King Henry get his crown Baltimore GM Eric DeCosta should be commended for pairing Jackson and Henry together back in 2024. Two of the most dynamic players at their position, Jackson and Henry powered the Ravens to a division title that season and came up a play short of playing for a trip to the Super Bowl. Things have changed since then, though. Baltimore missed the playoffs last year and will probably miss the postseason again this season. Respectively, Henry and Jackson will be 33 and 30 before the start of next season. Their championship window as teammates is closing, if it hasn't closed already. DeCosta should realize that he is beginning the process of turning over parts of his roster, including running back. Henry has been a great player for Baltimore, and DeCosta should reward him by giving him a chance to play for a contender. 
As noted above, Henry is a surefire future Hall of Famer. He's third all-time in career touchdown runs and is closing in on being seventh all-time in career rushing yards. Henry's career also includes being just one of nine players with a 2,000-yard rushing season. His 1,921 yards in 2024 (his first year in Baltimore) is the most in NFL history for a player over 30. Henry has done it all in his NFL career except get to and win a Super Bowl. Baltimore should give King Henry a chance to win his elusive crown before it's too late.

title: Ravens vs. Jaguars: Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? - CBS Sports
description: How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9
body:
How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:24 am ET
