            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars.Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first offensive play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts, winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year.Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Jaguars have the ballThe Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision.The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. 
The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler.Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington, who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks (Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented.
Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.)The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange. Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone.When the Ravens have the ballYou can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night.
Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once.Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football.Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night.
PredictionThe Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease.Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6

title: It wouldn't shock me if ... NFL Week 9: Chargers fire Mike McDaniel, another QB change in Arizona - CBS Sports
description: Is it finally over for Mike McDaniel in Los Angeles?
body:
Is it finally over for Mike McDaniel in Los Angeles?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:20 am ET

            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This is about the time on the NFL calendar when teams begin taking a hard look at themselves. With the arrival of Week 9, we're halfway through the regular season, and the Nov. 10 trade deadline is on the league's doorstep. That leaves every franchise facing the same question: What are we in 2026? Should we invest in the club we have or sell off pieces and begin building for a brighter tomorrow? The answer, of course, will vary from team to team. We could, however, start seeing some early indications of which way these clubs are leaning in response to that question as Week 9 unfolds. In our five predictions this week, three of them center around the trade deadline and/or facing the reality that 2026 is not their year and need to make moves to better themselves for 2027 and beyond. Meanwhile, there are a couple of other less existential developments that we wouldn't be shocked to see, including a rough showing from Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. We'll look to carry the momentum from a strong selection last week, where we accurately pinpointed a reduced snap share from Jonathan Taylor amid trade rumors and a strong performance from T.J. Hockenson. Below, you can find five storylines and/or individual performances that we wouldn't be shocked to see happen over the course of Week 9.  
Jonah Coleman silences Broncos trade chatter
The Broncos have been in the thick of trade rumors leading up to the Nov. 10 deadline as they've been a team eyed as a potential landing spot for some of the top available running backs. When you look at their 92.6 rushing yards per game average on the season, it makes sense why they'd possibly pursue the likes of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis, especially with the club sitting atop the AFC West and hoping to make another deep playoff run. However, that's a 10,000 ft. view of the situation in the backfield. If you zoom in, there's a possibility that the answer to their rushing woes is already on the roster. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a mini breakout performance in the win over Kansas City last week. In just his second game back from returning off injured reserve due to an ankle injury, Coleman saw a team-high 11 carries and rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown. He also caught four of his five targets for 63 yards, which included a pivotal 51-yard catch-and-run on the go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. 
That flash could just be the beginning for Coleman, who should continue to break out this week against Carolina. The Panthers are surrendering 4.8 yards per carry so far this season, which is tied for the fourth-highest in the NFL. Their 140.7 rushing yards per game allowed is third-highest in the league, so this is quite the matchup for Coleman. If he takes advantage of it, he'd silence any need for the Broncos to make a move for a back before the deadline. Carson Beck makes his NFL debut vs. Seahawks
The Cardinals made an in-game switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew last week, which helped springboard them to a win over the Cowboys. Minshew threw three touchdowns in the comeback win, which helped him be named the starter for Week 9 against Seattle. It also paved the way for the organization to trade Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. All of those moves have seen rookie quarterback Carson Beck quietly move up the depth chart. After initially serving as the emergency third quarterback, he's now the primary backup for Arizona. 
At some point, this ascension up the depth chart will continue for Beck to the point where he starts games for the Cardinals this season. After taking him atop the third round last spring, the organization has to see what it has in him before embarking on the offseason and possibly searching for another option under center. I wonder if Beck's debut could come as soon as this week during Sunday's divisional matchup with Seattle. 
Minshew slicing up a poor Cowboys defense is one thing, but he'll have a much more difficult challenge against a Seattle defense allowing the fewest total yards per game (250.0) through eight contests in team history. Their 4.2 yards per play allowed is also the fourth-fewest by any NFL team through eight games in the last 20 years. The Seahawks defense is also tied for the third-most takeaways in the NFL this season, so there's the possibility of things getting ugly for Minshew and the Cardinals offense. Does it get so ugly that Matt LaFleur makes another change in favor of Beck? I wouldn't rule it out. Jayden Daniels commits multiple turnovers vs. Rams
One of the underrated pieces of Washington's win over the Eagles in Week 8 was just how erratic Jayden Daniels was throwing the football. On the night, Daniels registered a 17.2% off-target throw rate, which is the third-highest single-game mark in his career (including playoffs). If that persists in this matchup against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Daniels' currently immaculate interception rate could shatter. 
Coming into Week 9, Daniels, who has been limited to five games due to an elbow injury, has yet to throw an interception. He's just the sixth player in NFL history to have at least 240 yards of total offense per game and zero interceptions through five starts. In fact, Daniels hasn't even lost a fumble, so he has no turnovers whatsoever so far in 2026. Something tells me that changes in Week 9. The Rams are tied for the fifth-most interceptions (7) on the season and are coming off a Week 8 win over the Chargers, where they picked off Justin Herbert twice and forced a fumble (recovered). Oftentimes, turnovers come in bunches, and if Daniels' throws continue to be all over the place, it could cost him. If the Rams, who are a 5.5-point road favorite, build a lead and force Daniels and the Commanders into a pass-heavy game script, it only adds more opportunity for the secondary to create multiple turnovers and stain his currently pristine record.  Bijan Robinson bounces back in a big way
Bijan Robinson enters Week 9 as the NFL rushing leader with 780 yards on the ground thus far. However, by looking at him over the last four weeks, you wouldn't really know it. Over the past four games, Robinson's rushing totals have taken a precipitous fall, averaging 4.4 yards per carry and 71.5 rushing yards per game. Those figures are well off the otherworldly pace he was on over the first four weeks of the year. 
Bijan Robinson in 2026First four gamesPast four gamesRushing YPG123.571.5Yards per rush5.84.4Rushing touchdowns40Week 9 presents a great opportunity for Robinson to get back to something closer to the production we saw over the opening month. Entering this international matchup in Madrid, Cincinnati is allowing 122.3 rushing yards per game, which is just outside the top 10 in the NFL. When you dig a bit deeper into the numbers, however, they're even more advantageous for Robinson, with the Bengals allowing 4.8 yards per carry (tied for the fourth-highest in the league). In a surprisingly tight win over the Titans last week, Cincinnati let Tony Pollard rush for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries. Joe Burrow has been one of the hottest quarterbacks in the NFL over the past few weeks, and one of the ways the Falcons could look to cool him off is by taking a ground-and-pound approach to this game. They have a back capable of taking over in Robinson, and this matchup is the perfect opportunity to take that approach. Expect a huge day for No. 7. Chargers finally fire Mike McDanielSunday goes one of two ways for the Los Angeles Chargers. I don't think it's out of the realm of possibility that they pull out their first win in this home matchup against the Texans, especially if Houston's defense continues to struggle. However, if it continues the way it has for LA and the offense can't muster anything close to a respectable unit, I think we've reached the point where McDaniel is let go. Yes, there were cases to make this move weeks ago, particularly during the club's Week 7 bye, but Jim Harbaugh elected to stick with his offensive coordinator. Coming out of the break, things didn't look improved whatsoever. In the Week 8 loss to the Rams, the offense continued to sputter. The unit ranks last in the NFL in points per game (14.1) and has the most total turnovers (17). They've also not scored a touchdown since the third quarter of Week 5. This season, the Texans defense hasn't been as ferocious as it was in 2025. They've allowed 30-plus points three times this season after doing so once in 2025 and have also allowed three 300-plus-yard passers after allowing zero last year. Even if Houston looks more like their 2025 version following the bye week, the optics of struggling against a beatable defense yet again will continue to bring things to a fever pitch with McDaniel. A loss would bring them to 0-8 on the season, and the club wouldn't play again until Nov. 16 when they are in Baltimore for a "Monday Night Football" matchup with the Ravens. That extended week could be another window for Harbaugh to make a change.

title: The Six Pack: Picks for Miami vs. Notre Dame, Alabama vs. LSU and lock of Week 10 - CBS Sports

Trust The Process in a Week 10 full of monster matchups

        This is the weekend of the college football season that everybody has been looking forward to since long before it began. Sure, a couple of the Big Games we expected aren't quite as big as anticipated over the summer, but others have emerged to take their place. There is no shortage of Big Games on the docket.Which makes it a little more difficult to determine the "Games of the Week" for this column. So before you start yelling at me for leaving your team's "Big Game" out of it, let me explain my process. In a typical week, there usually aren't more than three that would qualify. My usual tie-breaker in those scenarios is the rankings. The games with the highest-ranked teams get in.This week it's a bit different. You see, the way this column usually works is I break down the big games to the best of my ability, and then the other four games in the column are the games I feel best about from a betting perspective. This week I chose the two "big games" I feel best about from a gambling perspective.So, no, this isn't about disrespecting your conference or your brand. The Holy War between Utah and BYU, and Georgia vs. Ole Miss are top-10 matchups, but I'm not including them because I don't feel strongly about any aspect of those games from a betting perspective. But the top-15 game between LSU and the Alabama team damn near everybody thinks is overrated? Oh yeah, I've got strong thoughts on that one, so it made the cut!
Anyway, let's get to it.Games of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame: The announcement that Miami WR Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury that will keep him out a while certainly turned this game on its head a few days before kickoff, but while it changed the direction I originally planned to go, it did not change my reasoning much.Clearly, Miami's offensive ceiling drops without Toney in the lineup. He is a game-changing talent that Miami will have a very difficult time replacing, but it's not just the offense that will struggle. Miami's defense has been struggling for a while now, and this injury might make things worse.After allowing an average of 9.8 points per game in their first five, Miami's defense comes into this one having allowed 93 points in its last three games, and it's not like it was playing a murderer's row of great offenses in Florida State, Pittsburgh and North Carolina. None of them rank higher than 47th in points per possession, and North Carolina is the only one of the three that ranks in the top 65 in success rate (it's 31st). There's no excuse for Miami to be allowing as many big plays and touchdowns to those teams as it has.
And now that defense may be facing the prospect of being on the field a lot more. One of the benefits of having a great offense is it tends to give your defense plenty of rest. That's been the case with this Canes outfit, as Miami ranks fifth nationally in time of possession at 33:40 per game. Its average of 5.96 plays per drive ranks 33rd. The absence of Toney could prevent the Canes from being able to sustain the kind of clock-churning drives they've had all season.Well, if their defense has struggled keeping teams out of the end zone lately while only playing 61.13 snaps per game (30th fewest), what might things look like if they're out there more often?After all, this Notre Dame offense isn't exactly awful. It ranks third nationally in points per drive, fourth in success rate and has scored on 59.0% of its possessions (also third). While it struggled against BYU, that was on the road. Odds are things will be a bit different at home. The Pick: Notre Dame Team Total Over 31.5 (-104) at FanDuel

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU: Like most of you, I was surprised to see Alabama ranked as high as it is. I believe the ranking is a bigger indictment of the committee's process of putting teams in pods rather than looking at everybody as a whole, but whatever. There are a lot of games left, and Alabama will either win and earn that spot, or it won't, and everything will take care of itself.I'm leaning more toward the "it won't" side of things this weekend. Trust me, I'm a bit concerned about this one because I've been burned by LSU multiple times this season, but I don't like this matchup for the Tide. Keelon Russell looked good against Texas A&M last week, but the thing about Texas A&M is it stinks! Russell didn't look nearly as good in the losses to Georgia and Tennessee, and this is a very good LSU defense, particularly at home in this environment.The primary concern here is that Alabama's offense ranks 105th in pressure rate allowed. Now, a lot of that falls on Russell. He extends plays, and he does it in the good way. It's not that he's indecisive or panicking; it's that he can buy time with movement in the pocket and avoid the rush. But LSU's defense is sixth nationally in pressure rate and second in sack rate. This isn't the kind of pass rush you want to mess with, and we saw this be a problem for Bama when Russell was sacked nine times between the Georgia and Tennessee games. It put the offense in bad spots, and they couldn't overcome them often enough.
The one thing that would help Alabama's case is if LSU turns the ball over, and we all know Sam Leavitt has that in his bag. But -- But! -- Sam's done a much better job taking care of the football in recent weeks. The return of Trey'Dez Green and emergence of Jackson Harris have helped quite a bit in this department, and Alabama's defense has given up a lot of explosive plays in the passing game this year. The Pick: LSU -5.5 (-110) at FanDuelLock of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Michigan State at Michigan: Michigan's 28-21 win at Rutgers last week was not impressive, but the final score was a bit misleading. Michigan missed two field goals in the game, and had they made them, the game probably would have gone in a different direction. After all, the short field after the first missed kick immediately led to a Rutgers field goal. Those special teams issues could haunt us here, too, but another aspect of the game last week was that after a slow start, the Michigan defense shut down Rutgers for most of the second half, and new starting QB Tommy Carr looked much more comfortable running the offense.Now the Wolverines return home to face a Michigan State team that's running out of gas. The Spartans have lost six straight and have been dealing with a ton of injuries on defense. I'm sure the bye week helped, and you know Pat Fitzgerald is taking this rivalry game very seriously, but I just don't think the Spartans have the horses to keep this one close. Maybe it's iffy early, but it likely won't be late. The Pick: Michigan -13.5 (-106) at FanDuel
Fade of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati at No. 17 Houston: Football is a physical game that takes its toll on everybody playing it as the season goes along, and this is one of those times when Houston is catching Cincinnati at an absolutely perfect time. Houston had last week off to help it get over and recover from a tough 21-13 loss at Utah. Cincinnati didn't have that luxury. The Bearcats got their butts kicked by that same Utah team 49-25 last week. This was a week after their upset win over Texas Tech.Those are two very difficult opponents to play in consecutive weeks, and to then have to follow them up with a road trip to Houston to face another one of the Big 12's better teams is asking a lot of these Bearcats. Maybe they shock the world again, or maybe they run out of gas. I'm predicting the latter. The Pick: Houston -10.5 (-112) at DraftKingsPrinciple Play of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas State at Oregon State: You don't see nearly as many totals in the 70s these days as compared to years past, but it's not difficult to understand why this total is set so high. Oregon State is averaging 40.1 points per game, tying them with LSU for 7th in the country. Texas State isn't far behind at 38.1 points per game, which ranks 13th. And neither defense is all that good at stopping their opponents from scoring, either! In fact, the 32.0 points per game Texas State allows ranks 124th. Oregon State's rank of 71st (25.0) seems damn near stout in comparison.
So why am I betting the under? Is it because I'm an idiot? Well, sure, that's probably part of it, but it's not all of it. No, it's that Oregon State's offense has begun to slow down a bit in recent games and struggled against Fresno State last week. My theory is that there's enough tape out there on what they do now that opponents are at least better equipped to slow the Beavers down, even if they can't stop them. Also, Texas State's offense has been much better at home than on the road, scoring 1.67 fewer points per possession away from home. Finally, the weather could be a cherry on top. The forecast for the game, as I write this, calls for a high chance of rain and strong winds, with gusts up to 35mph. Granted, it's hard to rely on a weather forecast this far out from game time, but even if it's 55 without a cloud in the sky and light wind, I still think this total is too high. The Pick: Under 72.5 (-110) at FanDuelUpset of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio State: Two things can be true at the same time. Oregon can be one of the 2026 season's biggest disappointments, yet it's playing much better right now than it had been. Don't get me wrong, I don't believe firing the offensive coordinator magically fixes this team's issues, but it's hard to deny the Ducks looked much more cohesive on offense against Northwestern last week. The plan and attack made a lot more sense than what we'd seen in earlier games.Then there's Ohio State. While Buckeyes fans have been blaming everybody for last week's loss, my opinion is that the biggest problem they had was being forced to give a true freshman QB his first start on the road. Luke Fahey wasn't terrible, but he wasn't good enough to win the game. There's certainly room for improvement this week, and we may see it. After all, it's far easier to play at home than on the road when you lack experience. But this Oregon defense has played much better as of late, and while the Ducks are down to their backup QB, Dylan Raiola's far more experienced than Fahey. I don't think this line gives Oregon enough credit, and there's a much greater chance the Ducks pull off this upset than the number suggests. The Pick: Oregon (+245)

title: Miami's Malachi Toney expected to undergo surgery after injuring ankle in practice - CBS Sports
description: There is hope within the program that Toney's injury won't be season-ending
body:
There is hope within the program that Toney's injury won't be season-ending

        The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes got some concerning injury news on Wednesday when star receiver Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice. Sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that Toney suffered a high ankle sprain and is expected to undergo surgery, but there is hope within the program that Toney will be back in time for a potential College Football Playoff run.Toney is the Hurricanes' biggest offensive weapon with 73 catches, 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season, and his production for the nation's top team has made him one of the Heisman Trophy favorites alongside his quarterback, Darian Mensah. Losing Toney the week of Miami's biggest game would be a disaster for the Hurricanes, as the Miami offense looks for ways to create explosive plays against a talented Notre Dame defense. Toney's importance to the Miami offenseLast year's win over Notre Dame was Toney's breakout performance as a freshman, as he caught six passes for 82 yards and one touchdown in Miami's 27-24 victory to open the season. Toney is the top threat the Irish were going to have to game-plan and account for with multiple defenders, and any losing his ability to get downfield and move in space is a significant loss for Miami. 
Toney accounts for 35.1% of Miami's receptions, 38.6% of receiving yards and 46.4% of receiving touchdowns this season. Cooper Barkate is second on the team in all of those categories with 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns, and while talented, doesn't provide the same dynamic as Toney.The Hurricanes use Toney in myriad ways, and his ability to move around formations and alignments allows Shannon Dawson to attack different soft spots of defenses and prevents easy adjustments to what Miami is doing because of their variation. With Toney out, it allows the defense to focus more on slowing down Miami's run game. The Hurricanes are 21st in the country in rushing offense at 202.5 yards per game and are 10th in yards per attempt at 5.49. Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory make up one of the nation's best running back tandems, but they're made all the more effective by the respect defenses have to give to the big-play threat the passing game always presents when Toney is on the field. 
Notre Dame's defense figured to face the difficult choice of sending more bodies into the box to slow the run or keep help over the top to prevent Toney from getting loose. The ripple effects extend well beyond the Hurricanes' passing game. Heisman Trophy implicationsBeyond the impact Toney's injury will have on Miami's biggest game of the season, Saturday's game against Notre Dame figured to be Toney (and Mensah's) best opportunity to author a Heisman moment on a big national stage. Toney was second in the Heisman Trophy odds coming into the week at +290 at FanDuel Sportsbook -- only trailing Mensah at +170. After the initial injury news was reported on Wednesday, Toney dropped to +800 and after word broke he would have surgery he was off the board entirely. Toney's injury could also impact Darian Mensah's Heisman chances, as his passing productivity would likely take a hit if his best receiver can't play or is limited. 
As a result, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is back to the top spot in the odds at +160, Mensah is back to +165, and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr jumps to +550 in third as the Irish have moved out to a 7.5-point favorite over the Hurricanes. CBS Sports will continue to provide updates on Toney's status as the week progresses and more information becomes available.

title: Como scored nine at Lens, and it's no accident: Inside Serie A's Champions League stars - CBS Sports

                How Como became a Champions League team: Unique model, ownership power, Cesc Fabregas lead impressive rise
                
                    Francesco Porzio                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Only PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal have done better than Como after four Champions League matchdays. If that's not enough, they have a better goal difference than Barcelona, Manchester City and Liverpool, and more points than Bayern Munich or their Serie A rivals Inter, AS Roma and Napoli. You must be surprised, especially after Cesc Fabregas and his team won 9-1 away at Lens, one of the greatest wins in the European history of Italian soccer. Well, you shouldn't be. This is the result of a long-term project with a clear vision, a talented roster and one of the best emerging coaches in Europe. Here's what to know about this exciting team.
The coach: Cesc FabregasThe Spanish head coach joined Como as a player before retiring. He also started his coaching career at the club, taking charge of the Under-23 side and making a name for himself in the country. In the three years since becoming first-team head coach, Fabregas has clinched promotion to Serie A, a 10th-place finish in his first top-flight season and then Champions League qualification in his second full season in Italy's top flight. Beyond the results, Como have consistently showcased a clear tactical identity built around attacking football and an intense high press, delivering some of the most entertaining performances the league has seen in recent years. Fabregas has a clear footballing philosophy built around specific principles, and he is determined to achieve results without compromising his vision of how the game should be played. So far, he has managed to do just that.Fabregas is able to deliver results on his own terms thanks to the club's backing, further strengthened by his position as a minority shareholder. When Inter wanted to hire him to replace Simone Inzaghi in the summer of 2025, the club and the coach agreed to continue together despite interest from multiple clubs. Como president Mirwan Suwarso has spoken multiple times about the possibility of Fabregas leaving one day, knowing more clubs will knock on their door. At the same time, even for a coach as talented as Fabregas, it will be difficult to find another place like Como, where his views and decisions are not only welcomed but concretely supported. There aren't many clubs like that.The best player: Nico Paz When it comes to the players, there are multiple examples of how Como work in the transfer market, but Argentine midfielder Nico Paz is probably the one that best fits the club's vision. In the summer of 2026, Como signed him permanently from Real Madrid for around €60 million, a club-record fee, and extended his contract on a long-term basis.
Paz first joined Como in the summer of 2024, when the Italian club agreed a permanent deal with Real Madrid worth €6 million. The Spanish giants wanted to keep control of the player, though, inserting a 50% sell-on clause and the right to match any offer from another club. They also had the right to re-sign Paz in each of the following three summer transfer windows, for €9 million in the first year, €10 million in the second and €11 million in the third. Two years later, when Como moved to make his stay permanent, they agreed a deal worth around €60 million, while Real Madrid retained the option to bring him back in the summer of 2027 for €80 million.
This isn't just about one club doing a deal with another. It's also about the will of a player who wanted to stay at Como despite having the chance to return to Real Madrid. That says a lot about the potential of the project, as Paz is not just a talented midfielder but also the new face of Argentina after Lionel Messi retired from the national team earlier this year. In his four Champions League games so far, Paz has delivered three goals, including a brace against Manchester United, and five assists.
In other places or contexts, we would assume both Fabregas and Paz were just waiting for a better offer before moving on. At Como, the situation is different. The club have a long-term project and a model that could keep both of them there for many years, building something special and competing for major honors. Winning trophies is no longer just an ambition. It's becoming the club's next objective, and nights like the one against Lens are proof of that.

title: Why Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell should be on hot seat despite NFL-best 6-1 record - CBS Sports

body:
O'Connell's handling of his quarterback position and currently sagging offense merits a closer look

        The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) are in co-possession of the best record in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills and the San Francisco 49ers entering Week 9, the halfway point of the 2026 season. However, head coach Kevin O'Connell should be on the hot seat. How could both of those things be true? Let's take a quick look at what is powering the Vikings' early-season success and then take a deep dive into why O'Connell's bungling of his quarterback position -- both in 2026 and years prior -- in tandem with wasting Justin Jefferson and a poor playoff record should be causing his seat to be increasing in temperature.O'Connell is Minnesota's head coach and offensive play caller, but defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitzkrieg defense is why the Vikings have won six of their first seven games. Minnesota's defense leads the NFL in the following statistics:Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed)Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed)Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed)Completion percentage allowed (56.2%)Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8)Sack rate (11%)QB pressure rate (46%)Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century)However, O'Connell's offense is powered by 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Justin Jefferson, two-time Pro Bowl tight end T.J. Hockenson, former first-round pick wide receiver Jordan Addison, two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Kyler Murray and an offensive line that is allowing the fifth-longest time to pressure (2.71 seconds) in the NFL this season. Yet, it has scored 12 touchdowns. That is the fewest touchdowns by a team with a 6-1 record or better through seven games since Washington in 1982. 
The only team that has scored fewer touchdowns than the Vikings in 2026 is the winless Los Angeles Chargers with nine. Both the tanking Miami Dolphins (13 touchdowns) and the Deshaun Watson-led Cleveland Browns (13 touchdowns) have found the end zone more often than O'Connell's unit. That's embarrassing, and it's grounds for a potential coaching change come the offseason if things don't improve.Kyler Murray's fit in Kevin O'Connell's scheme The problem Minnesota has this season is that Murray isn't fitting well in O'Connell's scheme. Murray's -0.11 expected points added (EPA) per dropback is the fifth worst in the entire NFL, ahead of only Cam Ward (-0.12), Tanner McKee (-0.13), Daniel Jones (-0.19) and Justin Herbert (-0.22). 
O'Connell's offense thrived with Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold heaving the ball deep down the field to Jefferson and others over the middle of the field. Murray entered 2026 ranking 40th out of 45 qualified quarterbacks in throws of 10-22 yards (intermediate throws) between the numbers (over the middle of the field). That's why his connection with Marvin Harrison Jr. failed in Arizona. Murray much prefers throwing to the sideline with underneath completions to stay in rhythm. Just 10.7% of his throws in 2025 with the Cardinals traveled 10 or more air yards downfield, which ranked third among 42 quarterbacks with at least 150 passes last season. This season playing for O'Connell, 34.4% of Murray's throws are traveling 10 or more air yards, which is the 10th-highest rate in the NFL. That's why he is failing in Minnesota: Murray isn't a scheme fit, but O'Connell chose him anyway. However, the Vikings head coach is publicly in denial about how things are going with his squad, which ranks as the league's sixth-worst scoring offense (20.0 points per game). 
"It's going back through it. Any of the inconsistencies, really dive into the why. I don't necessarily believe it's going to be one tell-all thing," O'Connell told reporters postgame Sunday. "I think it's how we continue to put together the plans of where he's most comfortable in his alignment and then marrying the offense from there. I think we've done a good job of that."  Despite 10th overall pick J.J. McCarthy ranking dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) in his first full season as a starting quarterback in 2025, the Vikings offense was actually more efficient than it is now. Minnesota's playmakers know what the issues are. Jefferson left the locker room after the Week 8 loss without speaking to media members while Addison offered a direct assessment."It's not really about finding ourselves; it's just making routine plays," Addison told reporters postgame Sunday. "When you turn on the tape, we got guys open [in the pass game]. Running the ball, we got gaps that are open. We just got to execute honestly."

If O'Connell had the chance to sub in McCarthy for a struggling Murray to see if the former top 10 pick takes a leap after another year of season in his system. Instead, Minnesota chose to trade him away to the New York Giants in exchange for a bag of peanuts -- a 2027 fifth-round pick. Instead, all O'Connell has is a washed-up iteration of Carson Wentz and undrafted veteran Max Brosmer, a player with no touchdown passes and four interceptions across his seven NFL games. It took O'Connell and the Vikings a few years to make enough missteps to end up in this position. One could argue the merits of letting a 36-year-old Kirk Cousins walk in free agency. But Minnesota ended up pulling a rabbit out of the hat with Darnold a year after Kyle Shanahan and the 49ers rehabbed the 2018 NFL Draft's third overall pick while making him Brock Purdy's backup. Darnold piloted a Vikings offense that ranked No. 9 in scoring (25.4 points per game) as he threw for a career-high 35 passing touchdowns, the fifth-most in the NFL in 2024. Minnesota went 14-3 in the regular season but lost the de facto NFC North division title game in Week 18 against the Detroit Lions. Just a few weeks later, Darnold absorbed an NFL playoff-record nine sacks in a wild card round defeat against the Los Angeles Rams, souring O'Connell's perspective on his new Pro Bowl quarterback. Instead of building upon Darnold's successful 2024 season, O'Connell decided to let the 28-year-old walk in favor of McCarthy. As mentioned earlier, McCarthy was the NFL's cellar dweller in several metrics in his first year as a starting quarterback at football's highest level at 22 years old last season. Meanwhile, in Seattle, Darnold quarterbacked the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title, throwing five touchdowns and no interceptions in his new team's three playoff games, with only six sacks. That's just an average of two sacks per game in the Seahawks' championship run. Just like with Darnold, O'Connell decided to throw McCarthy away after one season of failure. Meanwhile in New York, McCarthy became the first Giants quarterback with at least five completions of 20-plus yards in consecutive games since Daniel Jones back in 2019. The Giants have also remained the NFC East's first-place team through eight weeks with a 4-2-1 record. Playoff failuresSince becoming the Vikings' head coach in 2022, O'Connell is 49-26, good for the fifth-best regular-season record in football, along with the 49ers. However, that has translated to just two postseason appearances (2022 and 2024) and no playoff wins. The two losses were the aforementioned faceplant against the Rams in the 2024 season and a 31-24 home loss against the Daniel Jones-led Giants. The next week, that same Giants team lost 38-7 at the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC divisional round.Two games isn't a massive sample size, but in both playoff games, O'Connell was clearly outcoached. Wasting Justin Jefferson Four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Justin Jefferson raced out to a historic start to his NFL career: His 7,432 yards receiving from 2020 to 2024 are the most in a player's first five seasons in league history. That production resulted in Jefferson averaging 96.5 receiving yards per game, which also ranked as the most ever in the NFL.   Then, J.J. McCarthy happened. McCarthy wasn't ready for the speed of the NFL game, ranking dead last in the entire league in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12), and passer rating (72.6) in 2025. His ineptitude led to Jefferson posting career lows in receiving yards (1,048) and receiving touchdowns (2) in 2025, which dropped his receiving yards per game average down to 90.2 -- the second-most in NFL history behind Puka Nacua's 95.3 average.Now, Kyler Murray is a poor scheme fit, which has Jefferson averaging a career-low 55.8 receiving yards per game in 2026. That's brought his career average down to 88.2 receiving yards per game. Jefferson still has a pathway toward being an all-timer -- he still has 8,815 career receiving yards through his first 100 games -- but he can see that path narrowing under O'Connell the last two seasons. That's why he let loose a rare display of public frustration on the sideline on Sunday.

The bottom lineSome team could soon be banging down Flores' door after the defensive masterclass he is putting together this season. That puts the Vikings in a spot where they may have to lose one of the best defensive masterminds in football next offseason. If Minnesota ends up missing the playoffs or fails to win a playoff game, wasting what is shaping up to be an all-time year from its defense, O'Connell would certainly face -- and earn -- heightened scrutiny.Perhaps there's a chance O'Connell's job could go to Flores by promoting him to be their head coach instead of losing him to another team. Regardless, O'Connell's lack of success in evaluating his quarterback position, despite his reputation as a "quarterback guru," along with wasting Justin Jefferson and a lack of results in the playoffs, deserves plenty of skepticism, 6-1 record be damned.
